title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: A student types "book the laser cutter tomorrow 3 pm". Your handler is: `info = ask_model(EXTRACT, text); slot = calendar.insert(info); return ask_model(CONFIRM, slot)`. Which description is right?

options.text: An agent, because the model's output supplies the values the later steps use
A workflow, because nothing the model returns changes which step runs next
An agent, because one request triggers two model calls and an API call
A workflow, because it makes only two model calls, fewer than an agent would

items.stem: Your code is: `while True: reply = call_model(messages); if reply.has_no_tool_request: break; result = run_tool(reply.tool, reply.args); messages.append(result)`. You wrote the `while` and the `break` yourself. Is this system a workflow or an agent? Answer with one word.

A fixed workflow answers each availability question with exactly 2 model calls. An agent version of the same assistant averages 6 model calls per question (5 tool requests, then the final answer). Assume every model call costs $0.003 and there are 800 questions per day. How much more does the agent version cost per day, in dollars?
A double booking wastes a student's whole lab session, so the calendar must be checked for a conflict before any booking is inserted, on every request. Which design should the team choose?

options.text: An agent whose system prompt says to check the calendar first
An agent with a check_calendar tool and a rule to retry on conflict
A workflow where code runs the check, then the model decides whether to insert
A workflow where code calls insert only when the check shows no conflict

items.stem: A log of 200 past API support tickets shows that every ticket needed an urgency label and then a customer-plan lookup. The 15% marked "unknown error" also needed anywhere from 2 to 14 log searches, each chosen from the last result. Which design is best for a small model budget?

options.text: One agent loop for the whole ticket, so every step stays flexible
A fixed workflow throughout, with the log search capped at three tries
Fixed code for the label and lookup, then an agent loop for the logs
An agent loop for the label and lookup, then fixed code for the logs

items.stem: Which of these tasks most needs an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Finding which of 40 manuals states a laser cutter's power limit, by searching and reading pages
Confirming a booking: check conflict, insert it, email the student, update the sheet
A nightly job that loops over tomorrow's bookings and has a model draft each reminder
Labelling each incoming question as booking, manual or other with one model call
